key_insight: A generalizable safety metric can be learned directly from large-scale, unlabeled naturalistic driving data to predict collision risk proactively, giving reliable real‑time warnings before crashes and near‑crashes.
problem_solved: Scalable, label‑free estimation of collision risk from everyday driving—addressing the lack of practical methods to quantify imminent danger and provide timely warnings for autonomous and assisted driving systems.
method: Use large-scale naturalistic driving data without explicit crash labels to learn a continuous, generalized collision‑risk measure via self-/proxy-supervised objectives.
Train models to score short‑term future trajectories in real time, producing rising risk signals that precede crashes and near‑crashes.
Validate at scale that risk score trajectories reliably provide lead time for early reaction, outperforming naive baselines in warning timeliness and reliability.
impact: Provides a label‑efficient, scalable approach for safety assessment that can be integrated into AV stacks and driver‑assist systems for earlier, more reliable interventions and for evaluating ML safety across diverse driving conditions.
visual_elements: Timeline plot showing risk score rising seconds before a crash/near‑crash (lead time visualization)
Map/trajectory heatmap highlighting high‑risk maneuvers and locations from naturalistic data
Performance chart (e.g., lead time vs. true positive rate or precision/recall) comparing the learned risk measure to baselines
Pipeline diagram: raw unlabeled drives → learning model → real‑time risk scoring → warning/mitigation
paper_title: Learning collision risk proactively from naturalistic driving data at scale
paper_authors: Yiru Jiao, Simeon C. Calvert, Sander van Cranenburgh, Hans van Lint
